headlines.title: Netflix's Regions Abroad Are All Growing Faster Than Its Home Market. I Don't Think That Makes the Stock a Bargain.
headlines.summary: Growth in the streaming giant's home region slid from 18% to 10% over just two quarters. Can the rest of the world make up for that?

headlines.title: What Could Netflix Stock Be Worth In Three Years?
headlines.summary: Over the past twelve months, Netflix (NFLX) stock has lost 40%, trailing the 17.0% return of the S&P 500. The shares now trade at 21.6 times earnings. That multiple sits well below what investors used to pay for them. Excluding readings above 100, the company's P/E averaged 39.7 at the last twelve quarter-ends. Yet the company's sales are still growing. So if Netflix keeps selling more, what would a share you buy today be worth three years from now.

headlines.title: Netflix, Inc. (NFLX) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It
headlines.summary: Recently, Zacks.com users have been paying close attention to Netflix (NFLX). This makes it worthwhile to examine what the stock has in store.

headlines.title: Why Goldman Sachs still backs Netflix despite falling viewership
headlines.summary: Goldman Sachs cut its price target but kept its Buy rating, pointing out a real growth engine for Netflix.

headlines.title: What Is Netflix (NFLX) Signaling With Its New Content Acquisition Chief?
headlines.summary: Netflix (NasdaqGS:NFLX) has appointed Craig Ferguson as director of content acquisition, effective early October 2026. Ferguson brings experience from senior content roles across major Hollywood studios, large tech platforms and digital distributors. His background includes leading content licensing and development teams focused on streaming, digital rights and multi platform distribution deals.

description: Netflix, Inc. provides entertainment services worldwide. The company offers television (TV) series, documentaries, feature films, games, and live programming across various genres and languages. It also provides members the ability to receive streaming content through a host of internet-connected devices, including TVs, digital video players, TV set-top boxes, and mobile devices. Netflix, Inc. was incorporated in 1997 and is headquartered in Los Gatos, California.
